==English== {{wp|+,+ (carriage)}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|brāk}}, {{IPA|en|/bɹeɪk/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-brake.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪk|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|break}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymid|en|slowdown}} [[Image:Disc brake.jpg|thumb|right|Disc brake on a motorcycle.]] Origin {{uncertain|en|nocap=1}}; possibly from {{bor|en|dum|-}} or {{bor|en|gml|brake||nose ring, curb, flax brake}}, which according to Watkins is related to {{m|en|brake#Etymology_4|sense 4}} and from {{der|en|gem-pro|*brekaną||to break}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alt|en|break#Etymology 2||rare}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A [[device]] used to [[slow]] or [[stop]] the motion of a [[wheel]], or of a [[vehicle]], usually by [[friction]] (although other resistive forces, such as [[electromagnetic]] fields or [[aerodynamic]] [[drag]], can also be used); also, the controls or apparatus used to engage such a mechanism such as the pedal in a car. {{defdate|from 18th c.}} #: {{ux|en|She slammed the '''brakes''' when she saw a child run in front of the car.}} #: {{ux|en|You’re pressing the '''brakes''' too hard—try just squeezing them.}} ## The act of braking, of using a brake to slow down a machine or vehicle ##: {{ux|en|Give the car a quick '''brake'''.}} ## {{lb|en|engineering}} An apparatus for testing the power of a [[steam engine]] or other motor by weighing the amount of [[friction]] that the motor will overcome; a [[friction brake]]. ## {{lb|en|figuratively}} Something used to retard or stop some action, process etc. # {{lb|en|military}} An ancient engine of war analogous to the [[crossbow]] and [[ballista]]. ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} The [[winch]] of a crossbow. {{defdate|14th|19th c.}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|_|nautical}} The [[handle]] of a [[pump]]. #: {{syn|en|swipe}} # A [[baker]]’s [[knead]]ing [[trough]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1617|author=Gervase Markham|title=Cavalarice the English Horseman|passage=You shall kneade{{...}}first with handes‥lastly with the '''brake'''.}} # {{senseid|en|animal-constraining device}} A [[device]] used to [[confine]] or [[prevent]] the motion of an animal. #: {{cot|en|chute}} ## {{senseid|en|horse-confining frame}} A [[frame]] for confining a [[refractory]] [[horse]] while the [[smith]] is [[shoe]]ing it. ##: {{syn|en|trave}} ## An [[enclosure]] to restrain cattle, horses, etc. ## A [[cart]] or [[carriage]] without a body, used in [[break in|breaking in]] horses. ## A carriage for transporting shooting parties and their equipment. ##: {{coi|en|{{w|shooting-brake|shooting-'''brake'''}}}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=It had been arranged as part of the day’s programme that Mr. Cooke was to drive those who wished to go over the Rise in his new '''brake'''.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1976|author=w:Terrance Dicks| title={{w|Terror of the Zygons#In print|Doctor Who and the Loch Ness Monster}}| chapter=1| page=11| passage=A few moments later they heard the sound of an engine, and a muddy shooting '''brake''' appeared on the road behind them.}} # That part of a carriage, as of a movable battery, or engine, which Compare {{cog|gml|brake||stump, branch}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A [[thicket]], or an area [[overgrown]] with [[brier]]s etc. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Venus and Adonis|passage=Rounds rising hillocks, '''brakes''' obscure and rough, / To shelter thee from tempest and from rain.}} #* {{RQ:Scott Marmion|passage=He stayed not for '''brake''', and he stopped not for stone.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1807|author=William Wordsworth|title=Poems|section=Fidelity |passage=He halts, and searches with his eyes
Among the scatter’d rocks:
And now at distance can discern
A stirring in a '''brake''' of fern {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Meredith Richard Feverel||5||The bird, with its fellow in the '''break''', drummed, and whirred, and to the misfortune of its species made its plumage seem a prize to them.}} =====Derived terms===== * [[cypress brake]] * [[canebrake]] * [[fernbrake]] =====Translations===== {{trans-top|thicket}} * Swedish: * Turkish: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} ====References==== * {{R:New English Dictionary}} * {{R:American_Heritage_Dictionary|brake}} ===Etymology 4=== {{etymid|en|tool}} Late {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|gml|brake}}, {{der|en|nl|braak}}, {{der|en|odt|braeke}}; possibly related to {{m|en|brake#Etymology_1|sense 1}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A [[type#Noun|type]] of [[machine#Noun|machine]] for [[bend#Verb|bending]] [[sheet metal]].
